name: Lobster Sauce
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: quarters of a pound of butter
ingredients.originalText: three quarters of a pound of butter

instructions.text: Boil a dozen blades of mace and half a dozen pepper-corns in about a jill and a half of water, till all the strength of the spice is extracted
Cut three quarters of a pound of butter into little bits and melt it in this water, dredging in a little flour as you hold it over the fire to boil
Toss it round and let it just boil up and no more
Take a cold boiled lobster and pound the coral in a mortar, adding a little sweet oil
Stir it into the melted butter
Chop the meat of the body into very small pieces and rub it through a cullender into the butter
Cut up the flesh of the claws and tail into dice and stir it in
Give it another boil up and it will be ready for table

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Boil a dozen blades of mace and half a dozen pepper-corns in about a jill and a half of water, till all the strength of the spice is extracted
2. Strain it
3. Cut three quarters of a pound of butter into little bits and melt it in this water, dredging in a little flour as you hold it over the fire to boil
4. Toss it round and let it just boil up and no more
5. Take a cold boiled lobster and pound the coral in a mortar, adding a little sweet oil
6. Stir it into the melted butter
7. Chop the meat of the body into very small pieces and rub it through a cullender into the butter
8. Cut up the flesh of the claws and tail into dice and stir it in
9. Give it another boil up and it will be ready for table
